correctness.rationale: A complete \(r\)-partite graph using exactly \(r\) colours has one colour per part. Necessity follows because fewer than \(r-1\) seeded parts expose at most \(r-2\) neighbour colours to every uncoloured vertex, so forcing cannot start. Sufficiency follows because an unseeded part, if unique, immediately sees all \(r-1\) other colours; once it is seeded, every remaining vertex sees all colours except its own. Counting nonempty subsets in seeded parts gives the generating polynomial, and replacing subset weights by the exact random-assignment weights gives the probability polynomial. The verifier exhaustively agrees on 224608 partial assignments across all 23 multipartite isomorphism types through order six.

value.rationale: The forced-colouring function is a recently developed graph polynomial whose evaluation is generally #P-hard for fixed palettes of at least three colours. The theorem gives a complete structural characterization, full size enumerator, probability polynomial, and minimum forcing-domain size on all complete multipartite graphs in the natural chromatic-palette regime \(r\ge3\). This is a broad classical family and a meaningful exact tractable case rather than an isolated numerical computation.
